Package hadur117.core.melee

Class MinimumRiskMovement

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.melee.MinimumRiskMovement
public class MinimumRiskMovement extends Object
Melee movement: minimum risk (MMOVE-1..4), the HawkOnFire and Diamond shape.

Each tick CANDIDATES points on a ring around Hadur are scored and the least risky becomes the destination; the current destination is kept until a point SWITCH_GAIN safer turns up or it is reached. The ring is capped at NEAREST_FRACTION of the distance to the nearest opponent, so Hadur never runs into anyone. Risk is in units of one full-energy opponent 100 px away, the sum of:

  • each opponent's energy (relative to Hadur's) over distance squared, doubled where Hadur would be that opponent's closest robot and half again for an opponent that hit Hadur in the last RECENT_HIT_TICKS ticks (MMOVE-2), and higher for points that run straight at or away from it rather than across it;
  • the virtual bullets: a head-on and a linear aim for every shot an energy drop showed, scored where they would be when Hadur gets to the point (MMOVE-3);
  • a pull off the middle of the field, a push off the walls' last few pixels, Hadur's recent positions, and a fixed per-round noise field, so the path is no pattern;
  • the melee strategy's posture (MMOVE-5).

On a team (T1) each living teammate whose position is fresh adds a term that rises with the inverse square of its distance from the point, taken where the teammate is predicted to be when Hadur gets there, and a term for a path that crosses its predicted track (MMOVE-6, MMOVE-7); the ring is capped by the nearest such teammate as by the nearest opponent; and each member's noise field and opening spot are shifted by its place in the roster (MMOVE-8), so five copies of this function do not choose one destination. Off a team none of this applies and the scoring is what it was.

For the first OPENING_TICKS ticks the closest-robot term doubles again and a pull heads for the nearest wall-adjacent spot away from the corners. With two opponents left the ring shrinks and the lateral weight rises (MMOVE-4), so the movement already orbits when the duel takes over. Everything is deterministic: the noise is a hash.

    MELEE_BULLET_SHADE
    MMOVE-20 (arm mbshade), inspired by ScalarR: with the surfer on, each of Hadur's own bullets in flight shades the stretch of every enemy wave it crosses, from the crossing outward, as a bot shadow does (MMOVE-18's share of Hadur's width).
    static final boolean
    MELEE_CLOSER
    MMOVE-14 (arm mcloser): off a team with three or more opponents left, an opponent's term is divided by one plus the number of other opponents nearer it than the point: a robot with closer prey is less likely to come for Hadur.
    static final boolean
    MELEE_DAMAGE_MEMORY
    MMOVE-22 (arm mdmg), inspired by Diamond's melee movement: off a team, each opponent's risk term weighs by the damage its bullets have done to Hadur over the whole battle, plus DAMAGE_BASE, times its mean distance from Hadur (a gun that hits from afar is the more dangerous), the weights scaled to average 1 over the living opponents.
    static final boolean
    MELEE_FULL_LATERAL
    MMOVE-23 (arm mlat), inspired by Diamond: off a team with three or more opponents, the lateral weight is FULL_LATERAL in place of LATERAL: a point reached straight at or away from an opponent counts double, not half again.
    static final boolean
    MELEE_HEAT
    MMOVE-13 (arm mheat): off a team, an opponent Hadur is the nearest robot to is assumed to fire at Hadur on the tick its gun could next be cool (from its last seen shot, else ASSUMED_FIRST_TICK) unless a real shot shows first: head-on and linear bullets at the power of its last seen shot (else ASSUMED_POWER), weighing ASSUMED_WEIGHT.
    static final boolean
    MELEE_HOPS
    MMOVE-12 (arm mhop): off a team with three or more opponents left, short hops: the rings run from HOP_INNER to HOP_SHARE of the nearest fresh opponent's distance, at least HOP_MIN and at most RING_MAX px.
    static final boolean
    MELEE_MIX
    MMOVE-16 (arm mmix), inspired by ScalarR: with the surfer on, a shot's share aimed at Hadur is Hadur's 1/d^2 from its source over the sum of 1/d^2 for every robot alive but the shooter, in place of MMOVE-11's 1/(1+k)^2; shares under MIX_FLOOR make no bullets.
    static final boolean
    MELEE_PATH_DANGER
    MMOVE-17 (arm mwpath), inspired by ScalarR: with the surfer on, each destination of the wave check scores (20 x its wave damage / all the damage in the air + c) x (1 + c), c its risk over the risk where Hadur stands, so a crowd both adds and multiplies.
    static final boolean
    MELEE_SEARCH
    MMOVE-21 (arm msearch), inspired by ScalarR: with the surfer on, the destinations it weighs are five SEARCH_STEP px steps (away from the crowd and toward the nearest corner; straight on; straight back; and square to either side) in place of the least risky points, each scored as the waves met on the way plus the least of the five steps from its end, two waves deep.
    static final boolean
    MELEE_SHADE
    MMOVE-18 (arm mshade), inspired by ScalarR: with the surfer on, a wave's danger at Hadur is cut by the share of Hadur's width that another robot nearer its source covers (each robot over SHADE_MIN px from the source, +-asin(18/d) wide).
    static final boolean
    MELEE_SURF
    MMOVE-15 (arm msurf), the melee surfer: off a team, the top three's way.

      MMOVE-15 (arm msurf), the melee surfer: off a team, the top three's way.       static int[] huntAssign(List<Point2D.Double> pack, List<EnemyInfo> enemies, long now)
      TMODE-13: each member's prey, as every member works it out from the positions they share. Members go in name order (me as name); each takes the fresh enemy of least (distance + PACK_ENERGY_WEIGHT x energy) squared, times HUNT_CROWD when HUNT_MAX_GROUP members already hunt it. Returns the members' places as indexes into enemies, in the order of pack; -1 with no fresh enemy.

      TMODE-6: a teammate screens Hadur from an enemy as another enemy does: each enemy's distance to its nearest other robot, which decides whether Hadur at a point would be its closest (MMOVE-2), takes the living teammates in view too (Ogi counts every robot nearer the enemy, teammates included).

    • waveBest

      Point2D.Double waveBest(List<Point2D.Double> candidates, MinimumRiskMovement.View v)
      TMODE-11, Ogi's wave check: the WAVE_RERANK lowest-risk candidates, and the destination held if not reached, are each driven to for WAVE_TICKS ticks, and every shot in flight that crosses Hadur's box on the way counts the share of it aimed there. A shot is a profile that sums to its aimed-at weight, not a certain bullet: its virtual bullets' headings share 1 - WAVE_UNIFORM of it, and the rest is spread over its escape angle. The score is risk / median(risk) + 3 x damage / max(0.1, median(damage)), each risk measured from the least of them (the posture term can make risks negative), times SWITCH_GAIN for the held destination.

    • surfBest

      MMOVE-15: the melee surfer's wave check, with MMOVE-17's scores and MMOVE-18's shadows when on.

    • steps

      List<Point2D.Double> steps(Point2D.Double from, MinimumRiskMovement.View v)
      MMOVE-21: the five SEARCH_STEP px steps from from, kept WALL_MARGIN inside the field: away from every opponent (each pushing 1/d^2) and toward the nearest corner (0.5/(500 + d^2)); along the way Hadur is heading (to its destination, else that first step); straight back; and square to either side.

      TMODE-27, Ogi's dodge: the TeamDodge.RERANK lowest-risk candidates, and the destination held if not reached, are each driven to through the shot profiles waves for WAVE_TICKS ticks and through the teammates' bullets for PATH_TICKS; scored as waveScores(double[], double[]), the held destination times SWITCH_GAIN.

      TMODE-11, TMODE-27: the rerank lowest-risk candidates, and the destination held if not reached, each driven to through the waves for WAVE_TICKS ticks and through the teammates' bullets for PATH_TICKS; scored as waveScores(double[], double[]), the held destination times SWITCH_GAIN. With ownFire the teammates' bullets add PATH_K times their damage to the risk, as PATH scores them, instead of joining the waves' damage.

    • pathBest

      Point2D.Double pathBest(List<Point2D.Double> candidates, MinimumRiskMovement.View v)
      TMODE-25, Firestarter's path check: the PATH_RERANK lowest-risk candidates and the destination held if not reached are each scored as their risk plus PATH_K times the damage of the teammates' bullets their drive would meet in PATH_TICKS ticks. The held destination keeps its place as in the plain choice: another wins only below SWITCH_GAIN times its risk, both with their bullet damage.

    • linesRisk

      TMODE-15: for each teammate, now, and its nearest fresh enemy, LINES_K where p lies on the line from the teammate through that enemy and past it, falling linearly to none LINES_HALF radians off the line as the teammate sees it, and none nearer the teammate than the enemy or more than LINES_REACH px beyond it. The bullets a teammate fires at that enemy and misses fly there.

    • gunLineRisk

      static double gunLineRisk(Point2D.Double p, List<Roster.Mate> mates, long now)
      TMODE-19: for each teammate whose stated aim is fresh and whose gun fires within GUNLINE_TICKS ticks, GUNLINE_K where p lies on the line from the teammate's place now along its gun heading, falling linearly to none GUNLINE_HALF px off it; only between GUNLINE_NEAR and GUNLINE_REACH px ahead. A lead shot flies there whether or not an enemy stands on it.
